item.title: US grants deportation reprieve to migrants from Ukraine and Sudan
item.description:
In late August, President Donald Trump's administration carried out its first deportation flight to Haiti since the Supreme Court allowed it to end temporary protected status (TPS) for the embattled country in June. "There are no extraordinary and temporary conditions in Haiti that prevent Haitian nationals…from returning in safety," the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) claimed in its TPS revocation, describing a country the State Department warns Americans not to visit "for any reason." The Trump administration has eroded America's humanitarian avenues, including TPS, which shields migrants from deportation. As a result, many noncitizens may become undocumented and could be forced to return to unsafe places. item.title: Tamara Keith and Carrie Dann on Trump's approval rating hitting a record low
item.description:
Overall, economic sentiment for Trump is poor, but small businesses seem fairly confident, according to several surveys There are 34m small businesses in the United States. They employ approximately half of the country’s workers and generate about half of the country’s GDP. They’re an important voting block. So how are they feeling about the economy as we head into November’s midterm elections? Overall, economic sentiment for Donald Trump is poor but small business – admittedly a diverse demographic that’s hard to poll – seems fairly confident. A number of recently published surveys and reports can help understand their mood. Confidence is generally stable. Continue reading...

item.title: Injured Ukrainian soldier rescued in first-ever drone evacuation mission
item.description:
Ukrainian forces used an aerial drone to lift a wounded soldier from the front lines in what the military says was the world’s first such battlefield rescue, newly released footage shows. The footage, shared Monday by Ukraine’s 92nd Separate Assault Brigade, shows the wounded soldier securing himself to a large drone before being lifted into the air and transported over blurred-out terrain, according to NBC News . The drone lowers him to the ground, where an operator greets him with, “Welcome back to the ground!” The video also blurs the faces of the operators involved in the mission, the outlet reported. He was marking the 43rd anniversary of Roe v. item.title: Wyoming Environmental Groups Debate Best Way to Manage Data Center Growth in the State
item.description:
A group of Texans believe they’ve discovered evidence that the state’s environmental regulatory agency has continued to issue permits to data centers despite Governor Greg Abbott’s call for it to stop. The nonprofits Public Citizen and FracTracker Alliance, working with local activists in Texas, looked through the public database of the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ) and discovered that the organization has worked on multiple permits for data center projects since Abbott called for a pause in the process on September 21. Abbott’s office denied approving any new permits in a statement to 404 Media. According to Public Citizen and the FracTracker Alliance, which cite documents publicly available on the TCEQ’s website, the agency has reviewed documents and assigned engineers related to more than a dozen permits related to data center projects in the state. item.title: France riots: AI photos falsely depict elderly couple ‘stripped and robbed’
item.description:
Protests over rising living costs and declining public services turned violent across France over the weekend, as more than 500,000 people took to the streets. Violent clashes broke out Saturday during nationwide demonstrations over rising living costs and poor school conditions. Hundreds of thousands marched across the country, while masked groups fought with police, looted businesses and set fires in several cities. Police reported 1,800 arrests nationwide, including 855 in the Paris region. VIOLENCE ERUPTS AT FRANCE PROTESTS AS MACRON WARNS UNREST IS BEING EXPLOITED The destruction was not limited to Paris. item.title: Houthi attack kills 53 in biggest single loss of life since Yemen civil war reignited
item.description:
More than 200 mostly young people said to be injured after ballistic missile attack on training camp for government forces At least 53 people have been killed in a Houthi ballistic missile attack on a training camp for Yemeni government security forces, making it the largest single loss of life since the country’s civil war reignited in September. The attack on al-Alam camp in the southern Shabwa province was said to have injured more than 200 others, mostly young recruits, and was described as a disaster by the country’s UN-recognised government. The injured were taken from the police and army training camp in the Jardan district to a hospital in the local capital, Ataq, where pleas for blood donations were made. Continue reading...

item.description:
